issues.description: The function/setup symbol 'setup_env' is described in the problem statement as being called with no parameters, but the solution implementation pushes an argument before calling it. Specifically, problem_statement.md instructs 'Rufen Sie `setup_env()` auf (keine Parameter)' (problem_statement.md lines 21-22). In solution_repository/helloWorld.asm the call sequence pushes a value then calls setup_env (lines 13-14: 'push 1' followed by 'call setup_env'), which indicates the solution expects a parameter. The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 5-8) declares 'extern printf' but does not declare or call setup_env, so students do not see an example extern or call-site to reconcile the instruction. This mismatch (no-parameter vs one-parameter call) can confuse students about the required call convention and whether they must pass an argument when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended calling convention consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the solution to match the problem statement by removing the pushed argument and the corresponding stack cleanup (remove 'push 1' and the matching 'add esp, 4' around the 'call setup_env'), and (optionally) add 'extern setup_env' to the template so students see the declaration. Alternatively, if a parameter is intended, update the problem statement to state the required parameter and add an example extern and push/cleanup sequence to the template. Prefer removing the push in the solution to match the current problem text.
